_status.summary: Re-checked existing dates with no changes and added the Disability Pride NYC Parade (Oct 18) and Bronx Halloween Parade (Oct 24).

ideas.text: Shoot down the avenue so the marchers fill the street with the steel of the elevated line overhead.
ideas.title: Costumes under the el

ideas.text: Frame a performer on stilts against the sky or the tracks with the heads of the crowd along the bottom edge.
ideas.title: Stilt walker above the crowd

ideas.text: Use a fast shutter on children reaching as candy is tossed from the parade.
ideas.title: Candy thrown

bronx-halloween-parade.name: Bronx Halloween Parade
bronx-halloween-parade.spot: Stand near Southern Blvd and Westchester Av before noon to catch groups lining up under the elevated tracks. Follow the parade to Bill Rainey Park for the performances after.
bronx-halloween-parade.where: Southern Blvd and Westchester Av, the Bronx, ending at Bill Rainey Park
bronx-halloween-parade.why: Stilt walkers, dancers, bands and costumed families parade under the elevated train in daylight, a week before the Village parade and with far smaller crowds.

ideas.text: From the rink edge, pan with one skater at a slow shutter so the crowd and lights streak behind.
ideas.title: Skaters in a blur

ideas.text: From the upper terrace, show the full rink with the skyline closing in on all sides.
ideas.title: Rink among the towers

ideas.text: Shoot through the glass of a market stall at a vendor or shopper lit by the warm lamps inside.
ideas.title: Faces in the stall windows

bryant-park-winter-village.name: Bryant Park Winter Village opening
bryant-park-winter-village.spot: The raised terrace on the library side looks down on the whole rink. Come on a weekday just after dark, when the stalls glow and the crowd is thinner.
bryant-park-winter-village.where: Bryant Park, 40 St to 42 St between Fifth and Sixth Av
bryant-park-winter-village.why: The rink and glass market stalls put skaters, shoppers and office workers in one small lit space surrounded by towers.

ideas.text: Watch for two people holding a sign-language conversation across the gap between marchers and the kerb.
ideas.title: Signing across the street

ideas.text: Pan with a wheelchair group at a slow shutter so the spokes and banners blur and the faces stay sharp.
ideas.title: Wheels rolling

ideas.text: Close in on stickers, flags and hand-lettered signs fixed to wheelchairs, walkers and canes.
ideas.title: Decorated chairs and signs

disability-pride-parade.name: Disability Pride NYC Parade and Block Party
disability-pride-parade.spot: Start at Madison Square Park at 11 am while groups assemble, then walk with the parade to Union Square for the block party.
disability-pride-parade.where: Madison Square Park to Union Square
disability-pride-parade.why: Marchers on wheels, with canes, guide dogs and hand-painted signs move slowly down a short route, which gives time to work close and talk to people.

ideas.text: Frame a group in traditional dress small in the lower third with the full wall of screens above them.
ideas.title: Saris under the billboards

ideas.text: Watch the dancers beside the stage for a last fix of a costume or a nervous glance before their turn.
ideas.title: Waiting to go on

ideas.text: After sunset, isolate one face lit by the colour of the billboards with the crowd soft behind.
ideas.title: Screen light at dusk

diwali-times-square.name: Diwali at Times Square
diwali-times-square.spot: Stand at the side of the stage on the Broadway plaza rather than in front, where performers wait and adjust costumes. Stay until dusk, when the screens start to light faces.
diwali-times-square.where: Broadway, 46 St to 48 St, Times Square
diwali-times-square.why: Dancers and families in bright traditional dress fill the plazas against the Times Square billboards.

dogparade.time: Steps off at 11 am; festival block 10 am to 4 pm
dogparade.where: Avenue B, 11 St to 7 St; festival block on 6 St between Avenues B and C

halloween.where: Sixth Av, Canal St to 15 St

ideas.text: Catch a small child in full costume looking up at a parent, or being carried when the walk gets long.
ideas.title: Costume and parent

ideas.text: Look for a costumed adult doing something ordinary, such as buying a coffee or checking a phone.
ideas.title: Monster at the bodega

ideas.text: Shoot down the avenue so the line of costumes runs between the shop signs and awnings.
ideas.title: Parade on 37 Av

jackson-heights-halloween-parade.name: Jackson Heights Halloween Parade
jackson-heights-halloween-parade.spot: Stand on the north side of 37 Av near the start at 89 St so the low sun lights the marchers from the front. Arrive before noon to see the groups line up.
jackson-heights-halloween-parade.where: 37 Av, 89 St to 76 St, Jackson Heights, Queens
jackson-heights-halloween-parade.why: A daytime neighbourhood parade of children and families in costume, with good light and far more room than the Village parade.

ideas.text: Fill the frame with marigolds, candles, sugar skulls and the framed photos people have left.
ideas.title: Offerings on the altar

ideas.text: Wait at the altar for someone setting down an offering and pausing for a second after.
ideas.title: Placing a photo

ideas.text: Isolate one person in skull face paint against the dark stone of the church.
ideas.title: Painted face

mano-a-mano-day-of-the-dead.name: Mano a Mano Day of the Dead
mano-a-mano-day-of-the-dead.spot: Go early on the first day while the altar is still being built and people are placing offerings. Work close to the altar and ask before photographing anyone leaving a photo of a relative.
mano-a-mano-day-of-the-dead.where: St. Mark's Church-in-the-Bowery, 131 E 10 St, East Village
mano-a-mano-day-of-the-dead.why: A large community altar with marigolds, candles and sugar skulls draws people who come to leave offerings, with live music and a Mexican market around it.

marathon.time: Wheelchair start around 8 am, runners in waves through late morning
marathon.where: Staten Island to Central Park through all five boroughs

thanksgiving.where: Central Park West at 77 St, south to Columbus Circle, then Sixth Av to Herald Square

veterans.where: Fifth Av, 26 St north to about 50 St
